note: Revenue-cycle, scheduling, workforce, pharmacy and data-quality lookups over the governed semantic tables (claim, claim_line, appointment, visit, clinician, medication, measurement) and received records.

rules.description: First-pass denial rate by payer or practice over a named period

plan.query: SELECT {group.col} AS {group.value}, count(*) AS claims, sum(first_status = 'denied') AS first_pass_denials, round(100.0 * sum(first_status = 'denied') / count(*), 2) AS denial_rate_pct FROM claim WHERE {period.where:service_date} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY denial_rate_pct DESC
plan.purpose: First-pass denial rate = claims whose first adjudication was a denial / claims, by {group.value}, service dates {period.start}..{period.end}

positives.question: What is our initial denial rate by payer for the last six months?
First-pass denial rate by practice in 2028

negatives: What is our initial denial rate by payer for the last six months, and why did it rise?
What is our initial denial rate by payer and reason for the last six months?

rules.description: Days from first claim submission to first payer cash, by payer
rules.pattern: ^(?:which payers take (?:the )?longest (?:to pay|from (?:claim )?submission to payment)|how long (?:does|do) (?:each payer|payers) take (?:to pay|from (?:claim )?submission to payment)(?:,? by payer)?) {period?}$

plan.query: SELECT payer, count(*) AS paid_claims, round(avg(julianday(first_payer_cash_date) - julianday(first_submitted_date)), 1) AS avg_days_submission_to_payment, max(julianday(first_payer_cash_date) - julianday(first_submitted_date)) AS max_days FROM claim WHERE first_submitted_date IS NOT NULL AND first_payer_cash_date IS NOT NULL AND {period.where:service_date} GROUP BY payer ORDER BY avg_days_submission_to_payment DESC
plan.purpose: Average days from first submission to first payer cash, per payer (claims with both dates; service dates {period.start}..{period.end})

positives.question: Which payers take longest from claim submission to payment?
Which payers take the longest to pay in 2028?

negatives: Which payers take longest from claim submission to payment and moved the most this month?
Which payers deny the most claims?

rules.description: Share of denied claims later paid, and the days from first adjudication to payer cash
rules.pattern: ^what (?:share|percent(?:age)?|proportion|%) of denied claims were (?:eventually|later|ultimately|subsequently) paid(?:,? and how long did (?:that|it) take)? {period?}$

plan.query: SELECT count(*) AS denied_claims, sum(denied_then_paid) AS eventually_paid, round(100.0 * sum(denied_then_paid) / nullif(count(*), 0), 2) AS eventually_paid_pct, round(avg(CASE WHEN denied_then_paid = 1 THEN julianday(first_payer_cash_date) - julianday(first_adjudication_date) END), 1) AS avg_days_first_adjudication_to_cash FROM claim WHERE ever_denied = 1 AND {period.where:service_date}
plan.purpose: Claims with any denial: share later paid (a denial followed by payment) and average days from first adjudication to first payer cash for those paid

positives.question: What share of denied claims were eventually paid, and how long did that take?

negatives: What share of denied claims were eventually paid by payer?
What share of denied claims were eventually paid and what were the reasons?

rules.description: Median and mean days from booking to the scheduled appointment, by specialty, practice or clinician
rules.pattern: ^what is (?:the |our )?(?:median|average|mean|typical) (?:lead time|days?|wait) from booking to (?:the )?appointments?(?: date)? (?:by|per|for each) {group} {period?}$

plan.query: WITH x AS (SELECT {group.expr} AS g, julianday(a.scheduled_date) - julianday(a.booked_date) AS v FROM appointment a LEFT JOIN clinician c ON c.clinician_id = a.clinician_id WHERE a.booked_date IS NOT NULL AND a.scheduled_date IS NOT NULL AND {period.where:a.scheduled_date}), r AS (SELECT g, v, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY v) AS rn, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY g) AS n FROM x) SELECT g AS {group.value}, max(n) AS appointments, round(avg(CASE WHEN rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) THEN v END), 1) AS median_lead_days, round(avg(v), 1) AS mean_lead_days FROM r GROUP BY g ORDER BY median_lead_days DESC
plan.purpose: Days from booking to scheduled date per appointment (one row per appointment_id), median and mean by {group.value}; scheduled {period.start}..{period.end}

positives.question: What is the median lead time from booking to appointment by specialty?
What is our average lead time from booking to appointment by practice in 2029?

negatives: What is the median lead time from booking to appointment by specialty for Medicaid patients?
What is the median lead time from booking to appointment by specialty next quarter?

rules.description: Visits per clinical day for each clinician, with specialty

plan.query: SELECT c.specialty, v.attending_clinician_id AS clinician, count(DISTINCT v.encounter_id) AS visits, count(DISTINCT v.event_date) AS clinical_days, round(1.0 * count(DISTINCT v.encounter_id) / count(DISTINCT v.event_date), 2) AS visits_per_clinical_day FROM visit v JOIN clinician c ON c.clinician_id = v.attending_clinician_id WHERE v.event_date IS NOT NULL AND {period.where:v.event_date} GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, visits_per_clinical_day DESC
plan.purpose: Per attending clinician: distinct encounters / distinct days with at least one encounter (a clinical day), grouped by clinician specialty

positives.question: How many patient visits per clinical day does each clinician see, by specialty?

negatives: How many patient visits per clinical day does each clinician see, by specialty, compared with benchmark?
How many patient visits per clinical day will each clinician need next month?

rules.description: Median and mean hours from the visit (note event time) to the signed note, by clinician or practice
rules.pattern: ^what is the (?:median|average|mean|typical) time from (?:the )?visit to (?:a )?signed note,? (?:by|per|for each) {group} {period?}$

plan.query: WITH x AS (SELECT {group.expr} AS g, 24.0 * (julianday(json_extract(payload, '$.signed_time')) - julianday(json_extract(payload, '$.event_time'))) AS v FROM record WHERE stream = 'notes' AND json_extract(payload, '$.signed_time') IS NOT NULL AND json_extract(payload, '$.event_time') IS NOT NULL AND {period.where:event_date}), r AS (SELECT g, v, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY v) AS rn, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY g) AS n FROM x) SELECT g AS {group.value}, max(n) AS notes, round(avg(CASE WHEN rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) THEN v END), 2) AS median_hours_to_sign, round(avg(v), 2) AS mean_hours_to_sign FROM r GROUP BY g ORDER BY median_hours_to_sign DESC
plan.purpose: Hours from the note's event time (the visit) to its signed time, median and mean by {group.value} (notes with both times)

positives.question: What is the median time from visit to signed note, by clinician?

negatives: What is the median time from visit to signed note, by clinician, and which are outliers after adjusting for volume?
What is the median time to close a patient telephone message, by practice?

rules.description: Average patient out-of-pocket amount per pharmacy-claim fill of a drug class, by payer

plan.query: SELECT json_extract(payload, '$.payer_id') AS payer, count(*) AS fills, round(avg(json_extract(payload, '$.patient_paid_cents')) / 100.0, 2) AS avg_patient_oop_usd FROM record WHERE stream = 'pharmacy_claims' AND record_id IN (SELECT record_id FROM medication WHERE source_stream = 'pharmacy_claims' AND drug_class IN {drug.in}) AND {period.where:event_date} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY avg_patient_oop_usd DESC
plan.purpose: Mean patient-paid amount (USD) per pharmacy claim of {drug.in}, by payer

positives.question: What is the average patient out-of-pocket cost per fill for insulin, by payer?

negatives: What is the average patient out-of-pocket cost per fill for insulin, by payer, and does it predict discontinuation?
What is the average patient out-of-pocket cost per fill for branded diabetes drugs?

rules.description: Patients in a population with a dispensed or claimed drug class, broken down by ingredient

plan.query: SELECT coalesce(m.ingredients, m.drug_class) AS drug, count(DISTINCT m.patient_id) AS patients FROM medication m WHERE m.drug_class IN {drug.in} AND m.evidence IN ('dispensed', 'claim') AND {period.where:m.event_date} AND m.patient_id IN (SELECT patient_id FROM patient WHERE {population.where}) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY patients DESC
plan.purpose: {population.text} with a dispensed or claimed {drug.in}, by ingredient (a patient on two ingredients counts under each)

How many patients with heart failure are on a beta blocker, by drug?

negatives: How many patients 65 and older are on a Beers-list medication, by drug and prescriber?

rules.description: Share of lab results carrying a LOINC code (received from the source vs mapped by the normalization dictionary)

plan.query: SELECT count(*) AS lab_results, round(100.0 * sum(loinc_source = 'source') / count(*), 2) AS loinc_received_from_source_pct, round(100.0 * sum(loinc IS NOT NULL) / count(*), 2) AS loinc_after_dictionary_mapping_pct FROM measurement WHERE source_table = 'labs'
plan.purpose: Lab result rows with a LOINC code as received from the source, and after mapping local names through the normalization dictionary

positives.question: What share of lab results in our data warehouse have standardized LOINC codes?

negatives: What share of lab results in our data warehouse have standardized LOINC codes by practice?
What share of claims have standardized codes?

rules.description: Distribution of office E/M levels (CPT 99211-99215) by rendering clinician or practice
rules.pattern: ^what is the distribution of (?:office |outpatient )?(?:e/m|e&m|evaluation and management) (?:visit )?levels(?: \((?:cpt )?99211-99215\)| \((?:cpt )?99212-99215\))?,? (?:by|per|for each) {group} {period?}$

plan.query: SELECT {group.expr} AS {group.value}, l.cpt AS em_code, count(*) AS claim_lines, round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY {group.expr}), 2) AS pct_of_unit FROM claim_line l JOIN claim c ON c.claim_id = l.claim_id WHERE l.cpt IN ('99211', '99212', '99213', '99214', '99215') AND {period.where:l.service_date} GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
plan.purpose: Office E/M claim lines (CPT 99211-99215) by code within each {group.value}, with each code's share of that unit's E/M lines

positives.question: What is the distribution of office E/M levels (99212-99215) by clinician?

negatives: What is the distribution of office E/M levels by clinician compared with their peers?
Which providers bill E/M level 5 visits far more often than their peers?

rules.description: Revenue codes on claim lines that carry no CPT/HCPCS code, with lines and billed charges
rules.pattern: ^which revenue codes (?:show up|appear|are billed) on claims? (?:lines )?without an? (?:cpt|hcpcs|cpt/hcpcs|cpt or hcpcs) code,? and how much is billed on them {period?}$

plan.query: SELECT revenue_code, count(*) AS claim_lines, count(DISTINCT claim_id) AS claims, round(sum(charge_cents) / 100.0, 2) AS billed_usd FROM claim_line WHERE revenue_code IS NOT NULL AND cpt IS NULL AND hcpcs IS NULL AND {period.where:service_date} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY billed_usd DESC
plan.purpose: Claim lines with a revenue code and neither a CPT nor a HCPCS code: lines, claims and billed charges by revenue code

positives.question: Which revenue codes show up on claims without a CPT/HCPCS code, and how much is billed on them?

negatives: Which revenue codes show up on claims without a CPT/HCPCS code, and why?
Which revenue codes are billed most?
